intro: Bandwar 2035 is a non-political development manifesto — 15 priorities identified by residents, 4 completed projects acknowledged by name, and a 10-year roadmap. This document is updated every year; completed priorities move automatically to the achievements record.

priorities.title: Chhath Ghat

required.caption: Proper Chhath Ghat with steps, railings, and lighting

priorities.reality: The village has no proper Chhath Ghat. Every year during Chhath Puja, hundreds of devotees — mostly women — stand on slippery, uneven riverbank steps of the Burhi Gandak to offer arghya to the setting and rising sun. There are no railings, no lighting, no changing rooms, and no safety arrangements. During the September 2025 flood, the riverbank eroded further, making access dangerous.
priorities.vision: A concrete ghat with safe, non-slip steps leading to the water. Handrails on both sides, separate changing rooms for women, LED lighting for evening and 4 AM aarti, CCTV surveillance, waste disposal bins, and a soak pit for ritual materials. A dedicated drinking water tap and first-aid station for the festival period.

how.authority: NMCG, BUIDCO, Gram Panchayat, District Administration

community: Volunteer labour for cleaning and leveling the ghat during off-season
Chhath Puja Committee can organise ₹500-1000 per household collection
Local businesses can donate for construction materials
A 5-member Ghat Monitoring Committee to oversee progress
Post-festival cleanliness drive involving youth groups

priorities.title: Ram Janki Fuels (Petrol Pump)

required.caption: Modernised pump with complete customer facilities

priorities.reality: Ram Janki Fuels serves the village and passing highway traffic on SH 55, but its facilities are minimal. There is no air pressure machine, no clean restroom, and no drinking water for customers. During summer, customers wait in the open sun. The convenience store is small and poorly stocked. There is no EV charging infrastructure for the future.
priorities.vision: A modern petrol pump with digital dispensers, a free air pressure machine, clean restrooms for men and women, an RO drinking water station, a small convenience store, an EV charging point, and a clean waiting area with benches. CCTV coverage across the forecourt and proper LED lighting under the canopy.

priorities.title: Ram Mandir Thakurbari

required.caption: Renovated temple with twin shikharas and full facilities

priorities.reality: The Ram Mandir Thakurbari is one of Bandwar's most distinctive temples, with its twin shikharas. But the temple needs renovation — the paint is faded, the courtyard is unpaved, and the facilities for devotees are minimal. During the annual Ram Katha, over a hundred villagers gather, but there is no proper seating, no sound system, and no clean toilets.
priorities.vision: A fully renovated temple with fresh whitewashed twin shikharas, marble flooring, LED evening lighting, and a sound system for Ram Katha and bhajan. A seating area for 100+ devotees, shoe rack and hand wash at the entrance, drinking water station, clean toilets, a secure donation box, and CCTV surveillance. A pucca room for the priest and a fire extinguisher for safety.

priorities.title: Chhota Krishna Mandir

required.caption: Renovated temple with fresh arches and marble

priorities.reality: The Chhota Krishna Mandir is the smaller of the village's two Krishna temples. Its distinctive scalloped arches and marble steps are its identity, but the paint has faded, the marble has worn out, and the shrine needs daily upkeep. During Janmashtami and Radha Ashtami, devotees visit in large numbers, but there are no proper facilities — no shoe rack, no hand wash, no seating.
priorities.vision: A freshly painted temple with bright, restored arches and non-slip marble steps. Clean marble flooring inside the shrine, LED evening lighting, fresh flower decoration daily, and a shoe rack at the entrance. A hand wash station, drinking water tap, secure donation box, and a small tulsi garden as part of the temple's spiritual ambience.

priorities.title: Bada Krishna Mandir

required.caption: Renovated temple with peacock motifs and paved forecourt

priorities.reality: The Bada Krishna Mandir is the larger of the two Krishna temples. Its whitewashed exterior, arched entrance, and courtyard handpump make it a key gathering place. But the paint has faded, the courtyard is unpaved, and there are no facilities for visiting devotees. During Janmashtami and Radha Ashtami, crowding creates safety concerns.
priorities.vision: A fully renovated temple with fresh white paint and blue trim, peacock feather motifs on the pillars (a symbol of Krishna), interlocking paver blocks in the forecourt, a green lawn on one side, and marigold flower pots. LED evening lighting, a sound system for bhajan, seating for 50+ devotees, and full facilities — shoe rack, hand wash, drinking water, and clean toilets. A secure donation box and CCTV surveillance.

priorities.title: Maharishi Gautam Aadi Shakti Durga Mandir

required.caption: Renovated temple with five shikharas and carved arches

priorities.reality: The Maharishi Gautam Aadi Shakti Durga Mandir is the village's principal Durga temple, painted in distinctive orange with green pillars. But the structure needs significant renovation — the walls need fresh paint, the carved details need restoration, and the temple lacks proper facilities for the large crowds that gather during Chaitra Navratri and Durga Puja.
priorities.vision: A fully renovated temple with five fresh white shikharas topped with gold kalash, intricate carved stone arches, and a green marble base cladding. Three decorated murtis inside the shrine. LED lighting for Chaitra Navratri, a sound system for bhajan and aarti, seating for 100+ devotees, and complete facilities — shoe rack, hand wash, drinking water, and clean toilets. CCTV surveillance and fire safety.

priorities.title: Chandrashekhar Chowk

required.caption: Renovated chowk with proper canopy and garden

priorities.reality: Chandrashekhar Chowk honours the memory of Chandrashekhar Singh, Begusarai's first communist MLA. The statue stands under a red-tiled canopy, but the surrounding area lacks maintenance — the pavement is broken, there is no seating for elders, and the evening lighting is poor. The chowk deserves to be a dignified public space.
priorities.vision: A properly maintained chowk with the statue under a fresh red-tile canopy, marble base, and steel railing. Evening LED lighting that illuminates the statue, a small garden around the pedestal, bench seating for elders, and non-slip paver block pavement. An information plaque explaining Chandrashekhar Singh's legacy, CCTV surveillance, and daily cleaning by the Panchayat.

priorities.title: Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar

required.caption: Fresh blue and gold gate with proper lighting

priorities.reality: Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar is the main entrance gate to the village, built in memory of a village martyr. The blue arch with 'Jai Hind' and 'Bande Mataram' is a source of pride, but the paint has faded, the gold lettering has worn, and there is no proper lighting at night. Pedestrians and two-wheelers share the same narrow road, creating safety concerns.
priorities.vision: A freshly painted gate in blue with gold lettering, topped with gold kalash finials. A tall flagpole with the Tiranga flying high, LED lighting on all four sides, and CCTV surveillance. The approach road is widened for two-way traffic, with a pedestrian footpath on both sides. An information plaque tells the story of Shaheed Ramchandra. A flower garden surrounds the base.

priorities.title: Historic Well (Chaupal)

required.caption: Fully restored well with heritage signage

priorities.reality: The historic well — the village's chaupal — has been given a fresh look with clean surfaces and modern lighting. But it still lacks proper drainage around it, seating for the elders who gather here every evening, and a heritage plaque that explains its significance to visitors.
priorities.vision: A fully restored well with a heritage plaque describing its history, stone-paved surroundings, and seating benches for 15+ elders. LED evening lighting, an iron jaali cover on top for safety, and tulsi and flower pots around the base. A designated photo spot for visitors and daily cleaning by the Panchayat. CCTV coverage for security.

priorities.title: Water Tower Coverage

present.caption: Jal Jeevan Mission water tower — partial coverage

required.caption: Complete piped water coverage to every household

priorities.reality: The Jal Jeevan Mission water tower has been built near the village fields, but the pipeline network is incomplete. Many households still depend on wells and handpumps. Water quality is not regularly tested, and there is no toll-free helpline for repairs. The September 2025 diarrhea outbreak exposed how critical this gap is.
priorities.vision: Complete pipeline coverage across the village with every household connected. Monthly water quality testing with public reports, chlorination at the tower, a toll-free repair helpline, and fair monthly meter reading. A grievance redressal counter at the Panchayat, backup power for the pump, and a water tanker for emergencies.

how.authority: Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), Gram Panchayat

priorities.title: Internal Roads

required.caption: Pucca road with drainage, footpath, and lighting

priorities.reality: The village's internal roads are unpaved. During the monsoon, waterlogging makes them impassable — children can't reach school, patients can't reach the main road, and farmers can't take their produce to market. During summer, dust affects the elderly and children. Several road projects have been sanctioned, but work is slow and some stretches remain incomplete.
priorities.vision: A fully pucca road connecting every ward to the main SH 55, with covered drainage on both sides, LED streetlights every 30-40 metres, and a pedestrian footpath with kerb stones. Yellow centre line on main roads, speed breakers near schools and the chowk, and rainwater harvesting pits every 100 metres.

priorities.title: Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya, Vandwar

required.caption: Modern school building with full facilities

priorities.reality: The government middle school — established in 1955 — operates from a pucca building. But the boundary wall is broken, there is no electricity in some rooms, and there is no separate toilet for girls. The school lacks a computer lab, a library, and a proper playground. Mid-day meals are not provided. The school's infrastructure does not meet the standards of 2026.
priorities.vision: A fully renovated pucca building with solar-powered classrooms, clean drinking water with RO, separate girls' and boys' toilets, a computer lab with 10+ computers, a library with 500+ books, and a playground with swings, slides, and a cricket pitch. A hygienic mid-day meal kitchen, a first-aid room with a resident nurse, a pucca boundary wall, and CCTV coverage.

how.authority: Education Department, BEPC, MP Office, Gram Panchayat

community: NRI diaspora support and local CSR

priorities.title: Gram Panchayat Bhawan

required.caption: Modern panchayat bhawan with digital services

priorities.reality: The Gram Panchayat Bhawan functions, but lacks modern facilities. There is no proper meeting hall for Gram Sabha, no digital service counter, and land records are not digitised. Citizens must travel to Begusarai for basic certificates. The building also lacks drinking water, clean toilets, and disabled access.
priorities.vision: An upgraded panchayat bhawan with a meeting hall for Gram Sabha (100+ capacity), a digital service counter (Common Service Centre), and digitised land records. Computers, printers, and internet access. Drinking water, clean toilets for men and women, and a ramp for disabled access. Permanent notice board, fireproof record room, and CCTV surveillance.

how.authority: Panchayati Raj Department, District Administration, MP Office

priorities.title: State Bank of India — Bandwar Branch

required.caption: Modern SBI branch with full customer facilities

priorities.reality: The SBI Bandwar branch is the village's only formal banking facility. It operates from a small building with limited counter space. During peak hours — especially on pension days and after harvest — long queues form outside. There is no proper seating for elderly customers, no dedicated counter for women, and no wheelchair access.
priorities.vision: An upgraded SBI branch with two or more counters including one dedicated for women, seating for 20+ customers, and air conditioning. A locker facility, a passbook printing kiosk, and a wheelchair-accessible ramp. Drinking water, clean toilets, and a digital display for rates and notices. CCTV surveillance and biometric authentication counters.

priorities.title: SBI ATM

present.caption: SBI ATM — single unit, frequent cash shortages

required.caption: Multi-ATM facility with cash deposit kiosk

priorities.reality: The village has only one ATM, which frequently runs out of cash. During festivals and harvest season, long queues form. There is no cash deposit facility, so villagers must visit the branch during working hours. The kiosk has no air conditioning, and security is a concern at night.
priorities.vision: A multi-ATM facility with at least two machines, a cash deposit kiosk (CDM), and 24x7 operation. LED lighting inside and outside, CCTV surveillance from multiple angles, and air conditioning. An emergency call button, fraud alert signage, and wheelchair-accessible entry. Backup power via UPS and generator.
